quote.text: Remember then that if you think the things which are by nature slavish to be free, and the things which are in the power of others to be your own, you will be hindered, you will lament, you will be disturbed, you will blame both gods and men: but if you think that only which is your own to be your own, and if you think that what is another's, as it really is, belongs to another, no man will ever compel you, no man will hinder you, you will never blame any man, you will accuse no man, you will do nothing involuntarily (against your will), no man will harm you, you will have no enemy, for you will not suffer any harm. If
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Recognize that, like in the quote, children possess their own nature; they must be allowed to grow by learning from their own experiences rather than being entirely controlled, thus fostering their true individuality.
    • Accept that while you guide, you cannot—and should not try to—possess every aspect of your child's development; by respecting their autonomy, you reduce conflict and promote healthier, more resilient relationships.
  • Leadership:
    • Understand that, as a leader, the focus should be on what lies within your control—your responsibilities and decisions—without overstepping into areas that inherently belong to others.
    • By setting clear boundaries and letting go of unwarranted control over external factors, you cultivate a work environment free of blame and foster a team that takes ownership of their contributions.
  • Product Management:
    • Apply the wisdom of distinguishing between what you can influence and what resides with others; channel your efforts into decision-making areas like strategy and design, while acknowledging external constraints and stakeholder needs.
    • By understanding that some aspects of the product or market conditions lie beyond your direct control, you can focus on building a collaborative, resilient environment that minimizes blame and maximizes innovation.
